sources.title: Search for UK Subsidies (the UK's statutory subsidy database under the Subsidy Control Act 2022): scheme SC11546 Northern Ireland Screen Fund, published 15 June 2026
sources.said: Subsidy control number SC11546 Subsidy scheme name Northern Ireland Screen Fund … Subsidy scheme status Active Public authority name Northern Ireland Screen … The Screen Fund is open to legally incorporated screen production companies that operate across one of the following 6 key sectors: large scale, television drama, animation and children’s, unscripted, independent film including feature documentary and games and 3D assets. … For production applications - letters of intent equalling at least 65% of the budget must be provided. … The Scheme will run from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2030. … Production awards primarily range from £25,000 for smaller scale projects up to £800,000 for television drama series and independent film. The exceptions to these levels of funding are large scale projects which can be up to £3 million and productions that have a high level of engagement with Northern Ireland creative talent, a substantial Northern Ireland economic return and/or a significant level of portrayal of Northern Ireland to an international audience. In these cases, the productions can be awarded higher levels of funding. … The majority of awards take the form of a repayable award, or in limited circumstances a grant. … On production awards the Screen Fund normally recoups its award pro-rata, pari-passu with other equity investors. Northern Ireland Screen typically takes a net profit position calculated as 50% of the overall Northern Ireland Screen contribution to the finance plan. … The annual budget of the scheme is up to £16,751,000 which results in a total maximum budget across the 4 year period of the scheme (April 2026-March 2030) of £67,004,000. … Maximum amount given under this scheme £3,000,000

figures.finding: A UK play's performer minimums by theatre. UK Theatre/Equity's Subsidised Theatre Agreement (performers at managers funded by the four arts councils): a performer's minimum salary at MRSL grades 1, 2 and 3 alike, £482.00 from 3 April 2023, £526.24 from 1 April 2024, £547.29 from 31 March 2025 to 5 April 2026 (the card's MRSL grade rows, £637.19 / £561.88 / £547.29, are another line, which the members-only agreement defines); no performer's rehearsal rate is printed apart. The agreement expired in April 2026 and was still in negotiation at Equity's update of 9 October 2026, so no 2026/27 rate exists. SOLT/Equity's West End agreement of 2026 to 2029: the eight-show ASM/performer minimum by the theatre's category, C up to 799 seats £790.30, B 800 to 1,099 £878.32, A 1,100 and over £965.55 from 6 April 2026 to 4 April 2027; £829.82, £922.24, £1,013.83 from 5 April 2027 to 2 April 2028; year 3 by March 2028's CPI plus 0.5% (2% to 5%); the card's ceiling salary during rehearsals is the same three figures; a twelve-show week is paid more. ITC/Equity (an ITC member's company): a minimum weekly salary of £601.00 in 2025/26 and £631.00 in 2026/27, the ITC's dates being financial years; a daily rate for three days or fewer.

ITC/Equity's directors: a preparatory fee of £1,916.75 for a full-length play (70 minutes and over) and £1,326.25 for a short play (70 minutes or less), and a weekly rehearsal payment of £601.00 (an artistic or resident director £730.00 a week for all duties); the downloadable sheet's 2026-27 column repeats the 2025-26 figures, and the ITC's dates are financial years.

figures.finding: The ITC's rates of pay page: "Please note, dates represent the financial year", so its 2026/27 and 2027/28 rates run from 1 April; the ITC/WGGB agreement came into effect on 2 June 2025 and revises its financial provisions before 1 April each year. The 2026-27 "agreed transition period" is told to ITC members only.

figures.finding: Creative Scotland's Open Fund: open to individuals and organisations based in Scotland in two strands, considered apart. 2024/25: individuals 535 awards of 1,761 applications (30%), organisations 153 of 365 (42%); theatre 90 of 281. The Open Fund for Individuals takes freelance and self-employed artists living in Scotland and at least 18, for £500 to £50,000; the organisations' strand £1,000 to £100,000.

The Arts Council of Wales publishes its project funds' ranges (Create and Engage up to £10,000 small and £10,001 to £60,000 large, £100,000 exceptionally, at most 90% of costs, the project mainly in Wales; Major Productions £100,000 to £300,000 from a £600,000 budget) and the Arts Council of Northern Ireland its National Lottery Project Funding's (normally £10,001 to £75,000 in 2026/27, 10% partnership funding); neither publishes how often a fund says yes, only whole-lottery counts (Wales 413 grants of 941 applications in 2024/25; Northern Ireland 430 commitments of 1,212 applications, which its account says aren't directly related).

Each nation's screen agency funds series made in its nation: Screen Scotland's Broadcast Content Fund (a single project, one-off or a series, normally half its budget spent in Scotland, at most £1,000,000; £4.751m spent in 2024/25) and Production Growth Fund (£200,000 to £500,000 for a high-end series spending ten times the award in Scotland); Creative Wales (74 projects funded since 2020, nine TV projects approved by March 2026); Northern Ireland Screen's Screen Fund from 1 April 2026 (awards usually £25,000 to £800,000 for television drama series, up to £3 million for large-scale projects, mostly repayable, letters of intent for 65% of the budget). None publishes how many series applied, so no rate of yes exists on the record.
